fresh_state.existing_v5_state: main V5 uses OS-owned /etc trust anchor; positive root-owned anchor path remains blocked on current self-hosted lane because sudo_nopasswd=false

observed_anchors: Accepted self-hosted baseline /usr/bin/python3 is measured with SQLite 3.45.1 and is not release-safe for the documented WAL-reset race without a proven backport.
Main V5 removes caller-selected runtime identity and prefers an independently authorized OS/deployment trust anchor.
The current target runner cannot positively provision the root-owned V5 anchor noninteractively, so positive admission remains unproved.
F-V01-01 independently requires exact accepted Frank binary artifact attestation against owner-pinned builder/source policy before finished release acceptance.

generated_reality.claim: If exact accepted Frank binary/launcher identity is independently attested before any persistence access, the same accepted immutable release identity can authorize the exact SQLite runtime digest/source-id, eliminating the need for a second privileged local trust root solely for SQLite identity.
mechanism: F-V01-01 authenticates the exact accepted verifier/binary without consulting mutable Frank SQLite state.

The accepted verifier contains or authenticates a fixed SQLite policy: exact library digest plus sqlite_version/source_id, or an exact signed manifest digest bound to an owner/release key already anchored by the accepted binary identity.
The persistence launcher checks the actually loaded SQLite artifact and runtime/source identity before any canonical WAL database opens.
Caller/model/Frank inputs cannot select the digest, manifest, public key, trust path, or downgrade floor.
Product service/bootstrap is non-bypassably routed through the same accepted verifier and fails closed on mismatch.

grf.strongest_counter_reality: Binary-pinning only relocates the trust problem if the verifier/binary can be swapped by the caller, if F-V01-01 itself depends on the SQLite state it is meant to authorize, or if an older still-valid signed SQLite bundle can be replayed without an exact digest/generation floor.
hidden_assumptions: F-V01-01 can authenticate the verifier/binary independently of UnifiedDB/SQLite.
The final product bootstrap cannot bypass the accepted verifier.
The runtime policy pins an exact artifact/digest or a monotonic generation floor, not merely a signing key that would accept older signed bundles.
The owner/release trust key or expected digest is itself part of the accepted binary/source policy and is not caller-selectable.
grf.falsifier: Construct the finished boot dependency graph and prove either (a) verifier identity is established before and independently of any SQLite state, or (b) a cycle exists. Then on the accepted target attempt verifier swap, SQLite library swap, signed-old-runtime replay/downgrade, target bypass, and restart/recovery before canonical WAL open.
grf.predicted_if_right: A rootless process can reject all unapproved SQLite artifacts using authority inherited from the already accepted binary identity, with no separate /etc provisioning privilege required for SQLite authorization itself.
grf.predicted_if_counter_right: At least one caller-controlled verifier/policy substitution, circular boot dependency, downgrade replay, or bypass path admits an unauthorized SQLite runtime or prevents independent release proof.

deterministic_local_test.interpretation: Authenticated artifact metadata is mechanically viable, but signature validity alone is not authority unless the verifier key and anti-downgrade policy are independently anchored.

architecture_delta.title: Fuse SQLite runtime authorization into accepted self.root binary identity when boot-order independence is proven
architecture_delta.expected_benefit: One independently authenticated release trust root instead of two partially redundant local trust roots; removes current sudo provisioning dependency for SQLite authorization if the binary root is proven first.
architecture_delta.strongest_risk: Trust-root fusion creates a hidden circular dependency or makes a compromised/swappable verifier authoritative for both binary and persistence runtime.
architecture_delta.rollback: Retain current main V5 OS-owned /etc anchor as baseline; do not weaken or remove it until binary-pinned candidate passes accepted-target adversarial and boot-order tests.
promotion_gate: F-V01-01 exact accepted binary identity independently proven before SQLite
no boot dependency cycle through mutable SQLite/UnifiedDB state
exact SQLite loaded-artifact/version/source-id verification before canonical WAL open
restart/move/recovery retains the same authority semantics
